correctness.rationale: Connectivity and degree are inductive; bipartite regular children have equally sized unique color classes. Counting exactly \(2((m/2)!)^2\) admissible out of \(m!\) cross permutations yields conditional \(p_k\); the independent-child square recurrence and exact-duplicate linear recurrence follow by independence of new matchings. Conditioning preserves the corresponding independent/copy dependence structures and gives independent uniform orientation choices at genuinely independent nodes. Central-binomial Stirling expansion has summable \(O(2^{-k})\) errors, giving both sharp logarithmic limits, the convergent correction gamma and duplicube second-order terms. Standard finite connected graph period and Perron–Frobenius equivalences establish the spectral statement. Exhaustive 24 and 80,640 finite matching checks, rational recurrence checks and numerical expansion checks ran from the provided standalone program; none replace asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: The event that a non-lazy walk remains periodic, equivalently the extreme negative adjacency eigenvalue survives, is a natural global stochastic graph invariant directly motivated by current random-walk research. The two canonical recursion couplings share many typical geometric properties but have sharply separated rare-event entropies: \((\log 2)n2^n/2\) versus \((\log 2)2^n\). Exact all-dimension products quantify a real structural dependence effect rather than a manufactured finite slice. The conditional matching law identifies the exceptional bipartite graph ensemble for further study of conditional spectra and mixing. These exact facts go beyond existing high-probability qualitative nonbipartiteness and are mathematically useful independent of a broad downstream theorem.
